wa_mcloughlin_canyon_tonasket.blurb: McLoughlin Canyon lies a few miles south of Tonasket in the Okanogan, with the Okanogan River close by. The cliffs are gneiss, and the climbing leans toward sport with a solid minority of trad and a couple of top-rope lines. Grades of 5.9 and 5.10 make up the bulk, with easier routes at the bottom end and a handful at 5.11. Last Wall holds the most climbs: a long, mostly bolted face looking east. Main Wall, also east-facing, mixes trad lines with newer sport routes, while South Buttress faces south and southeast and carries multi-pitch sport. Little West Canyon is a small side canyon with bolted lines. Late winter through spring and fall are the comfortable seasons; summer runs hot, though the east-facing walls catch morning shade.

wa_rocks_of_sharon.blurb: Rocks of Sharon is a cluster of outcrops on a ridge south of Spokane Valley, near Tower Mountain, with views across the Palouse toward Steptoe Butte. Reaching the rock takes a steady uphill walk of roughly twenty minutes. Sport routes dominate, with a good number of trad lines, a few top-ropes and a small set of boulder problems. Most routes fall between 5.9 and 5.11, with moderates below and a few 5.12s above. Big Rock is the centerpiece and holds the most climbs, and the area includes multi-pitch routes. The Rookie Wall, just south of Big Rock, is the gentler option, and the Bird Watching Boulder and the Triplets add more sport lines.

az_munchkinland_area.blurb: Munchkinland sits high on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains near Tucson, at roughly 7,000 feet. Sport routes outnumber trad, and most climbing falls between 5.9 and 5.11, with a few easier lines and some 5.12. The season runs roughly April to October, and shade is plentiful enough that it cools quickly as winter nears. The Towers, the Wall of the Marching Munchkins and the Wall of the Dancing Dwarfs face roughly west and stay shaded until around midday. The Wall of the Trundling Trolls holds the most climbs and is mostly trad on crack systems, in compact stone with few loose holds. The Wall of the Waltzing Witches offers moderate sport.

ca_cattle_pocket_and_corridors_area.blurb: This area is in the Alabama Hills near Lone Pine, on the Eastern Sierra side of California. Cattle Pocket is a wall of towers above the road, and the Corridors are a series of rock blades running north to south beside its entrance. Sport routes outnumber trad, with a couple of top-ropes, and the grades are weighted heavily toward 5.10 with a good spread of 5.7 to 5.9 below it. Besides Cattle Pocket and the Corridors, the area includes Lost Eye to the Moon, Zoo Wall and Dinosaur Cracks, where trad is the main style at the last two.

ca_cedar_grove_boulders.blurb: Cedar Grove Boulders are in Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Park, at the bottom of Kings Canyon beside the South Fork of the Kings River. The valley is glaciated, with tall granite walls and waterfalls above, and summers are hot. The bouldering is spread along the road between the park entrance and Road's End and is described as lightly developed, with room for harder problems. Nearly everything is a boulder problem, mostly V0 to V3, with fewer at V4 to V6. Roads End holds the most climbs, followed by the Graveyard Boulders, with smaller groups at Zumwalt Meadows North and the North Dome Boulder field.
